t: You're at Finsbury Square, a small square of about 1.7 acres in central London, with a six-rink grass bowling green. It was developed in 1777 on the site of older green space known as Finsbury Fields, and it sits on the east side of City Road, opposite Bunhill Fields. Moorgate station is about 200 metres south. The explorer James Clark Ross was born here. He became a Rear-Admiral and explored both the North and South Poles, taking part in Arctic expeditions with his uncle John Ross and with William Edward Parry, and leading his own Antarctic expedition from 1839 to 1843.
